content: Approximately 4% of patients may experience elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels greater than five times the upper limit of normal (ULN), while 1% may experience elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels exceeding five times the ULN. Increased tearing (lacrimation) has been reported in 1% of patients. Some patients may develop symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, characterized by an inability to stand without support after lying down for five minutes. If patients experience dizziness or lightheadedness following administration, they should lie down until symptoms resolve. Patients with onchocerciasis who are co-infected with Loa loa may develop serious or potentially fatal encephalopathy after treatment. Moxidectin has not been studied in patients co-infected with Loa loa. Therefore, patients who require treatment and have been exposed to Loa loa-endemic areas are advised to undergo diagnostic screening for loiasis before initiating therapy. Patients with hyper-reactive onchodermatitis (sowda) may have an increased likelihood of experiencing severe edema and worsening of onchodermatitis following moxidectin treatment. These symptoms should be managed with appropriate symptomatic treatment in affected individuals. There is limited data on the use of moxidectin in pregnant women, and the available information is insufficient to determine whether there is an associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage. Moxidectin has been detected in the breast milk of lactating women following a single dose. However, there is no data on the effects of moxidectin on breastfed infants or milk production. In preand postnatal studies conducted in rats, oral administration of moxidectin at doses less than twice the recommended human dose (based on body surface area) during the lactation period resulted in adverse clinical signs, weight loss, and increased mortality in rat pups. These findings suggest that moxidectin in lactation milk was responsible for the adverse effects. Due to these serious findings, women are advised not to breastfeed during treatment and for seven days after treatment. Moxidectin is generally considered acceptable for use, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, the exact mechanism of action against Onchocerca volvulus is not fully understood. Moxidectin is active against the microfilariae of O. volvulus. The drug is excreted primarily in feces (2% unchanged) and has a clearance rate of 5 L/hr. It can be administered as a single dose with or without food. Moxidectin tablets should be stored at temperatures below 30°C (86°F) and protected from light. Once the container is opened, the full contents should be used within 24 hours, and any unused portion should be discarded.
